decision.why: Three independent bug fixes in separate modules (body parsing/validator, compress, secure-headers). Each is a small local change with an existing test suite to verify against, so none needs deep tier.
decision.shared: Run the relevant tests with: npx vitest --run <test file paths>. Do not commit.

parts.title: Case-insensitive Content-Type media types in parseBody() and validator()
parts.text: `parseBody()` and `validator()` match Content-Type media types case-sensitively. A request with `Content-Type: Application/JSON` or `Application/X-WWW-Form-Urlencoded` is parsed fine by the platform Request, but Hono's checks skip it and pass an empty object downstream. Media types are case-insensitive (RFC 9110), so these requests should be parsed and validated like their lower-case equivalents.
parts.why: Two call sites need the same case-insensitive media type check; ordinary fix with a clear reproduction and existing tests.

parts.title: Pass 206 Partial Content through compress middleware uncompressed
parts.text: The compress middleware gzips 206 Partial Content responses. The Content-Range header still describes the uncompressed byte range, and the original Content-Length is dropped, so clients that stitch ranges together get corrupted data. A 206 response should be passed through uncompressed.
parts.why: Single-module, one-condition change; the behavior is clearly specified, so low effort suffices.

parts.title: Secure-headers nonce when both CSP and report-only policies are set
parts.text: In the secure-headers middleware, using a nonce in one CSP mode breaks when both `contentSecurityPolicy` and `contentSecurityPolicyReportOnly` are set: for example a static enforced policy plus a report-only policy that uses a nonce. The request ends in a 500 response. Each policy should work independently, including when both use nonces.
parts.why: Small change in one middleware but reasoning-heavy about how two policies share nonce state; raise effort, not tier. Risk area is sized as usual and reviewed at deep.
